summary: Remote agent runner: WebRTC-driven Claude/Codex shell execution on installer host
details: The package is a headless daemon that lets remote Factiii web/mobile clients drive Claude/Codex agent CLIs — which in turn run shell commands, git operations, tmux sessions, and builds — on the installer's host over a WebRTC data channel brokered by the hardcoded signaling host https://api.factiii.com. The tarball also ships four prebuilt frpc (fast reverse-proxy) binaries under vendor/ (darwin/linux x amd64/arm64), consistent with the advertised share-a-port capability via dev.factiii.com. The remote-control capability is the documented product function: pairing uses a JWT with AES-256-GCM session keys stored in the OS keychain, the daemon starts in the foreground via `factiii-runner start` (or an optional user-installed LaunchAgent/systemd user unit), and the control plane is an outbound WebRTC connection rather than an open listening port. Network bytes from the paired remote peer end up driving shell execution and full-host actions on the installer's machine, including when a watchdog keeps the daemon alive across terminal close. No install-time execution, no credential scraping of ~/.aws / ~/.ssh / ~/.npmrc, no env-var dumps, no secondary undisclosed channel, and no fetch-and-execute of remote code were observed. The static POST hits in dist/cli.js are consistent with the documented signaling and API traffic to api.factiii.com rather than a covert exfiltration endpoint.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
